newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schering first-half profit up, outlook improves.
newsitem.headline: Schering first-half profit up, outlook improves.

text.p: Schering AG, the world's largest maker of oral contraceptives, said Thursday its sales and profits surged in the first half due to higher volume sales of gynecological products and its Betaferon multiple sclerosis drug.

Schering said group sales increased by 21 percent to 3.1 billion marks ($1.6 billion), due in part to the inclusion of two new units acquired in late 1996, while pre-tax profit rose 20 percent to 498 million marks ($264 million).
Sales of Schering's Betaferon, one of a few drugs sold around the world to treat the chronic progressive disease of the central nervous system, rose 24 percent to 327 million marks ($173 million).
"Naturally we would like to repeat this success in the second half," Schering chief financial officer Klaus Pohle told Reuters.

Despite increased competition from rival Biogen, maker of the drug Avonex, Schering said Betaferon sales in the United States rose to 154 million marks ($82 million) during the six-month period, with the number of patients overall remaining stable.
Schering said it anticipated a rise in profits of up to 20 percent for the year, in part due to the weak mark helping to boost the value of foreign sales.

"We expect that sales will continue to develop positively in the second half of 1997, further supported by the sustained rise in exchange rates of currencies important for us," Schering said in a statement.
The gynecological products unit, helped by the acquisition of Finnish group Leiras and Germany's Jenapharm last year, and the therapeutics unit made up two-thirds of Schering's total sales.
Without the two acquisitions, which manufacture fertility control and hormone therapy products, Schering said total sales would have risen only 11 percent.
Despite the robust sales growth, Schering reported a 5 percent drop in sales in its diagnostics unit to 770 million marks ($408 million) from 814 million marks ($431 million) in the year-ago period.

Schering said the unit, which manufactures x-ray contrast products, came under increased pressure from competition and prices but was still able to expand its business in contrast agents for magnetic resonance imaging.

Pohle also said Schering was seeking to broaden its product range, a complaint from some investors since Schering is so focused on fertility control and hormone therapy for women. He noted increased research spending in the second half.
